label: START D4
title: No rivastigmine for Lewy body or Parkinson's disease dementia
statement: Rivastigmine for Dementia with Lewy Bodies or Parkinson’s disease dementia.

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: START names rivastigmine for dementia with Lewy bodies or Parkinson’s disease dementia. When no supply is recorded, check whether another cholinesterase inhibitor is already treating the dementia.

medicine_groups.name: Medicines that meet this criterion: rivastigmine
medicine_groups.note: Rivastigmine includes the skin patch and the capsules. Donepezil and galantamine do not count for this criterion. Generic capsules or patches labelled with rivastigmine and a company name count too.

needs_facts.what: Dementia with Lewy bodies, or Parkinson's disease dementia

rule_for_models: Apply only when the record establishes age 65 years or older. Suppress the finding if the record gives an end-of-life palliative focus, a contraindication to the proposed therapy or another valid clinical reason for its omission. Donepezil or galantamine alone does not clear an otherwise qualifying finding. Ask for a review of the current treatment and the reason for omitting rivastigmine. Avoid suggesting duplicate treatment. Suspect a finding when the record holds a line for dementia with Lewy bodies or Parkinson's disease dementia and no rivastigmine (Group A, including capsules and transdermal patches) is supplied in the last six months of the record; cite the condition line. When rivastigmine is supplied in the last six months, there is no finding. A Yes from the pharmacist confirms that at least one qualifying diagnosis is present. A No confirms that neither is present, so there is no finding. Another dementia diagnosis alone does not qualify. A coexisting dementia diagnosis does not cancel a qualifying diagnosis. A Not known answer leaves the diagnosis unresolved unless the record already establishes it. A medicine for Parkinson's disease alone does not show dementia, so with no dementia line make no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Supplies alone cannot show whether the person has dementia, its type, an end-of-life palliative focus or a contraindication to rivastigmine. They may also omit a previous trial stopped for nausea, a slow heart rate or a patch reaction, a choice by the person or family to decline treatment, or supplies from another pharmacy or hospital.
ask_the_gp: Whether rivastigmine is suitable for this person, or has already been tried and stopped.
